title: unified-rollouts-probing-weighted-shadow-canary-autorollback-workflow
author: Ava Chen
description: Summary: Add a probing-driven weighted shadow + canary rollout workflow and automated rollback policy to unified rollouts. Motivation: some customers require staged probing of new model variants via shadow traffic followed by a weighted canary once probes pass; when probe or canary metrics regress we need deterministic automated rollback and clearer observability hooks. This PR implements: 1) a new ProbingScheduler that drives lightweight probe traffic against shadow variants with configurable probe cadence and sample size; 2) WeightedShadowProbe rollout strategy which accumulates probe success metrics and gates transition to weighted canary; 3) metric-driven autorollback integration that evaluates multiple signals (latency p95, error-rate, quality-regression from prompt-evals) with configurable thresholds and cooldowns; 4) e2e tests and stability guards to avoid flapping and to ensure safe backoff; 5) console UI and docs updates for configuring probe/canary/rollback policies. Checklist: - [x] design doc linked (ENG-3145) - [x] implementation of scheduler and strategy - [x] unit tests for core logic - [x] e2e tests simulating probe->canary->rollback - [x] perf benchmark run and mitigations - [x] docs and console changes - [x] security review

review_comments: Diego Morales: Overall design looks good. Two questions: (1) how do we avoid probe amplification when autoscaling reduces capacity? (2) Can probe traffic be rate-limited per-route?

Ava Chen (author): For (1) the scheduler respects capacity signals and reduces probe concurrency by default; the cooldown/backoff ties into autoscaler signals. For (2) yes, we added route-level rate limits and a per-route probe cap in rollout config.
Priya Patel: The autorollback evaluator currently uses absolute thresholds. Recommend supporting relative/regression thresholds for quality metrics to avoid false positives on noisy baselines.
Ava Chen: Added support for relative delta thresholds and updated evaluator unit tests to cover regression detection.
Ethan Li: Unit tests look good. e2e tests are a bit flaky on CI (integration-e2e) when perf-bench runs concurrently. Can we isolate e2e to a dedicated runner?
Ava Chen: Split e2e into a dedicated integration job and added tagging to avoid concurrent perf runs. CI updated accordingly.
Marisol Gomez: Small nit: console label i18n keys missing for new fields.
Ava Chen: Added i18n keys and a follow-up small PR will include translations.
